intents.hardship: The customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss.
intents.dispute: "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product"; a claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is also a dispute.
intents.already_paid: "I already paid": only a payment of this past-due amount.
intents.restructure: A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments.
intents.vague: A vague period: "next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes".
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

quotes: A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal.
A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt.
Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
rules.opening_is_attempt.derivation: Refusing the opening ask (pay today) uses an attempt, and attempt 1 is a separate proposal on the last business day of the week; the band counts (1 and 2) are the proposals after the opening ask, so opening_is_attempt is false.

rules.opening_blocks_repeat.assumption: The brief does not say the opening ask counts as a repeat; default false.

rules.skipped_repeat_counts.assumption: The brief only says not to repeat a refused offer; the engine default applies.

quotes: If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once.
Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.
rules.too_much_floor.derivation: The single floor offer takes the place of attempt 1 (floor on attempt 1's date); only attempt 2 may name the floor again, so the floor offer is attempt 1.

quotes: When the attempts are used up, stop.
A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt.
If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
If it fails, try once more.
Offer to connect them with the customer support team.

rules.deadline_adjust.assumption: Deadlines are the n-th business day after today, so they are always business days; the default previous_business_day applies to any other computed date.

rules.first_ask.derivation: The first ask is the full past-due amount today.

quotes: From Monday 2 November 2026, close a refused call with outcome `no_promise` and reason `declined_offer` instead of `refused`.

changes.assumption: No dated value change; the CM-01 holiday (2026-10-23) is undated and is in the base calendar.

assumptions: The facilities handbook pages are not collections rules and were ignored.
Memo CM-01 (undated) adds Friday 23 October 2026 as a non-business day; it is in the base holiday list together with the playbook holidays.

Memo CM-02 replaces the credit card floor: 40% of past_due, rounded up to the next whole dollar, then at least 50 dollars, and never more than the debt (a debt below 50 has the whole debt as floor). Because of this, credit_card is left out of floor_field; personal and car loans keep instalment_amount.
If 40% of past_due is already a whole dollar amount, it is not rounded further (up_unit).

Memo CM-03 is a dated change of the reason code: refused calls on or after 2026-11-02 close as no_promise / declined_offer. This also covers rule 45 (not wanting to talk after verification), which uses the refused event.
too_much_floor is attempt_1: the single floor offer of rule 26 takes the place of attempt 1, and attempt 2 (late band) names the floor again on the deadline.
max_unclear is omitted because the brief does not say how often an unclear answer to a payment question is asked again.
after_promise.ask_anything_else is left at the default true; the brief is silent.
Brief A never uses add_note, so notes are disabled and every note code is empty.
Callbacks for 'today' are not restricted to business days; only 'the next business day' is.
A date given only as numbers is read day-month-year (date_order dmy) and sent as YYYY-MM-DD.
The credit card floor is called 'minimum amount' in speech, because it is no longer the minimum_payment field.
